title: fix(post): Heidenhain DIN/ISO stops for a manual tool change
body:
## The defect

On a tool change, the DIN/ISO post (`assets/posts/heidenhain.cps`) wrote only `T<n> G17 S..` and `M3`. It wrote no retract and no stop. On the Fehlmann Picomax 55 (iTNC 530, NC 340490-03) this is unsafe:

- The machine file states `tooling.tool_change = "manual-retract-top"` (a manual change).
- MP 7480.0 = 1: TOOL CALL only gives the T number to the PLC. TOOL CALL does not stop.
- MP 7440 bit 0 = 0: the program halts at M06.
- MP 950.2 / MP 4210.0: the tool change height is M92 Z-0.05 (`Z+0 M92` = the top of traverse range 1).
- The programming manual changes a tool with `L Z+0 R0 FMAX M92`, then an M6 move (p. 2-11, p. 2-19).

A multi-tool DIN/ISO program therefore ran on with the old tool in the spindle and the new tool's length active. The engine did not refuse it: it only passed `toolChangeMode` to the script.

## What changed

1. **DIN/ISO post, on the verified `manual-retract-top` installation.** At each tool change the post writes this sequence (from the golden):

   ```
   N220 M5*                         (end of the previous section, as before)
   N230 ; OPERATION: Second contour - 2D CONTOUR*
   N240 G00 G90 Z+0 M92*            (retract, under the OLD tool call)
   N250 M6*                         (the change call of the machine's manual)
   N260 ; CHECK DRIVES OFF BEFORE TOUCHING TOOL*
   N270 ; CHECK QUILL AT PHYSICAL CHANGE POSITION*
   N280 ; ABORT IF EITHER CHECK FAILS*
   N290 ; THEN INSTALL TOOL 3 FLAT-6*
   N300 M0*                         (the stop: halt, drives off)
   N310 ; T3 FLAT-6 - FLAT END MILL D6*
   N320 T3 G17 S3500*               (the new length becomes active here)
   N330 M3*
   N340 G00 G40 G90 Z+10*           (first move with the new tool)
   ```

   - At the first tool, the tool in the spindle is unknown. The post writes `M6`, the checks and `M0` only, with no move (the same as the first `M0` of the Klartext post).
   - A repeated tool number is not a change. It gets no stop.
   - Plain `manual` states no change position. The post does not claim it, and the engine law refuses the pair.
2. **Installation check (#4114 review).** The retract and the stop are safe only with the machine parameters of one installation. The DIN/ISO post refuses by name each `manual-retract-top` machine that is not that installation: controller identity `iTNC 530` / `340490-03` AND machine model `Fehlmann Picomax 55 (iTNC 530)`. This is the same check as the Klartext post (`heidenhain-klartext.cps` `onOpen`). The post stops with a script error, and nothing is written. The refusal text:

   `Heidenhain TNC: the manual-retract-top tool change (M92 retract, M6, M0 stop) is verified only on the Fehlmann Picomax 55 (iTNC 530) with iTNC 530 NC 340490-03; the machine <model> states <identity, or "no controller identity"> - choose a post that is verified for this installation`
3. **`M0` after `M6` (#4114 review suggestion, taken).**
   - With `M6` alone, the halt depends on MP 7440 bit 0 = 0. A service change of that parameter does not change the machine file or the identity, so the identity check cannot see it. `M0` halts whatever that parameter says.
   - On the Picomax, `M0` also switches the drives off (manual p. 1-17). The stop where the operator installs the tool is now the stop that switches the drives off.
   - The Klartext post stops with `M0` at the same point.
   - `M6` stays, before the checks: the machine's manual writes it for the change.
   - Cost: the program can halt two times at a change (at `M6` by the parameter, then at `M0`).
4. **Engine law** (`crates/post/src/post/manual_change.rs`, called in `engine.rs` before any hook). On a machine with `tooling.tool_change` = `manual` or `manual-retract-top`, a script must list that mode in its manifest: `manualToolChange = ["manual-retract-top"]`. If it does not, the engine refuses by name, with the post and the machine.
   - `heidenhain.cps` and `heidenhain-klartext.cps` declare `manual-retract-top`.
   - No shipped post declares plain `manual`. Thus each shipped post is refused by name on a user machine that states plain `manual`.
   - `assets/posts/AGENTS.md` documents the manifest word, and that a script that lists a mode also refuses each installation that its sequence was not verified for.

## Why the active tool length is safe

- The T block comes after the stop, not before the retract as in the Fehlmann manual. Thus the retract runs under the old tool call: the length in force is the length of the tool that is in the spindle.
- The retract target is machine-referenced (M92). If the control ignores the tool length for an M92 move, the quill goes to the change height. If it applies a length, the target is above the range-1 limit and the control stops with a limit error. With the verified installation's parameters, the move goes only up in both cases. On a different installation these parameters are unknown, so the post refuses it (item 2).
- The section end already wrote `M5` (and `M9` when coolant was on) before the retract.
- The first move with the new tool comes after `M0` and after the new T block.
- `docs/decisions/4085-heidenhain-din-manual-change.md` records this, the installation check, the `M0` decision and the dropped options.

## Post × machine pairs

The only shipped machine with a manual tool change is `fehlmann-picomax55.mch` (`manual-retract-top`). All other shipped machines state no `tooling.tool_change`, so the law never asks them and their output does not change.

| Post on the Picomax | Before | After |
|---|---|---|
| `heidenhain-klartext.cps` | posts (M0 stops) | posts, byte-identical (declares the mode) |
| `heidenhain.cps` (DIN/ISO) | posts with no stop (the defect) | posts with the M92 retract, M6 and the M0 stop |
| all other shipped posts | posted with no stop, or refused for another reason (kind, dialect) | refused by name by the manual change law |

The test `every_shipped_post_without_the_manual_change_is_refused_on_the_picomax` reads `assets/posts/` and pins this table.

## Pinning tests

`crates/post/tests/script_heidenhain.rs`, module `picomax` (joins the existing suite):

- `din_iso_retracts_and_stops_before_the_second_tool_moves`: the golden `recorded/golden/heidenhain/picomax_two_tools.nc`, and a structural assert: `M5` < retract < `M6` < `M0` < new T block, no move between the retract and the T block, a stop with no move before the first tool.
- `din_iso_refuses_a_manual_change_machine_it_was_not_verified_for` (new, #4114): the Picomax file with no controller identity, with other NC software, with another control model, and with another machine model. Each is refused by name. It failed on the previous head (checked with that head's `heidenhain.cps`).
- `the_same_tool_again_is_no_change_and_writes_no_stop`.
- `an_automatic_change_writes_no_stop` (the same machine with `changer`).
- `every_shipped_post_without_the_manual_change_is_refused_on_the_picomax` (the table above; plain `manual` refuses the DIN/ISO post).

Unit tests in `manual_change.rs`: `a_manual_machine_needs_the_declared_mode`, `an_automatic_or_unstated_change_never_asks_the_manifest`.

`crates/post/tests/machine_controller.rs`: its test script `FACTS` declares `manualToolChange` (it posts on the Picomax and on a `manual` copy).

## Goldens

- New: `crates/post/tests/recorded/golden/heidenhain/picomax_two_tools.nc`. On the new head it has one `M0` block after each `M6`, and the block numbers after the first `M0` move by 10 and then by 20.
- Moved: none. Automatic-change and machine-less output is byte-identical.

## Not exercised

- No run on the real control (NC 340490-03). The DIN/ISO post is verified only on the 606425-04 programming station (#3095). The `G00 G90 Z+0 M92` block form, the halt at `M6` and the drives-off at `M0` come from the manual and the machine parameters, not from a run.
- The behaviour of the Picomax PLC when `M6` comes before the new T block is not known. The checks and the `M0` halt stay correct in both cases.
- A mid-program start ignores M06 stops (MP 7680 bit 3). This PR does not change that.

## Gate

Final head `6ad78aafd` (logs `gates/4114-6ad78aafd-{quick,light,clippy,heavy}.log`, first line `6ad78aafd435c3b8cdff1615cf7dc1c49fad429b`):

- `cargo xtask gate quick --base origin/main`: 310 steps, 0 failed, 0 stalled (includes `script_heidenhain`, `script_heidenhain_klartext`, `machine_controller`, `klartext_builtin`, `example_catalog`, `example_catalog_adaptive`, `example_catalog_edge_work`).
- `cargo xtask gate light`: 6 steps, 0 failed.
- `cargo clippy -p camcraft-post --all-targets -- -D warnings`: clean.
- Targeted heavy step (P1, safety floor): `cargo xtask gate heavy --base origin/main --only "app heavy: example_catalog"`: ok. No heavy test posts on a manual change machine; this binary posts the shipped examples through the changed post and engine.

The Klartext manifest line is on the existing `workOffsetMax` line, so the Klartext refusal goldens (they quote script line numbers) stay byte-identical. This is kept as is; a later change to the Klartext header must keep the line count or regenerate those goldens.

Changelog: The Heidenhain DIN/ISO post now retracts with M92, writes M6 and stops with M0 at each tool change on the Fehlmann Picomax 55 (iTNC 530, NC 340490-03, manual tool change at the upper position); it refuses by name each other machine that states this manual tool change. A post that does not write a manual tool change is refused by name on a machine that states a manual tool change (`manual` or `manual-retract-top`).

Effort: high

🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)

Fixes #4085
